title: ‘Highest priority’: Centre responds to Neha Bora ahead of Delhi-NCR toxic air protest

ai.summary: The Centre responded to All India Students’ Association president Neha Bora's request for an urgent meeting with the environment minister on Delhi's air pollution crisis, stating the minister is prioritizing pollution control but currently in Turkey for COP31.

facts.claim: The Union environment ministry responded to an email from AISA president Neha Bora
facts.quote: The Union environment ministry responded late on Sunday evening to an email from All India Students’ Association (AISA) president Neha Bora, asserting that minister Bhupender Yadav attaches the "highest priority" to tackling air pollution in Delhi-NCR and is continuously monitoring enforcement measures across states.

facts.claim: The minister is currently in Turkey leading the Indian delegation at COP31
facts.quote: In an email to Bora, who has asked people to head to Yadav’s Jor Bagh office on Monday afternoon, the ministry also noted that the minister is currently in Türkiye leading the Indian delegation at the COP31 climate summit.

facts.claim: The ministry said the minister is continuously monitoring and reviewing measures taken by state governments
facts.quote: In its response late on Sunday, the ministry said Yadav was "continuously monitoring and reviewing" the measures taken by state governments and local authorities.

facts.claim: The ministry directed NCR states to ensure strict, time-bound enforcement of air pollution measures
facts.quote: In his last meeting with the Delhi NCR states held on November 11, the NCR states have been directed to ensure strict, time-bound and coordinated ground-level enforcement including deputation of secretary-level senior officers in each city of Delhi NCR states to closely monitor the enforcement actions

ai.background_note: The Delhi-NCR air pollution crisis has led to citizens demanding action, with protests planned to reach the environment minister's office.
